newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait parliament to reopen missile deal with UK.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait parliament to reopen missile deal with UK.

text.p: Kuwait's parliament is expected to reopen a debate over plans to buy British surface-to-surface missiles worth some $90 million, Western diplomatic sources said on Wednesday.
"A group of deputies want to question the defence minister about picking the British missile and dropping a cheaper French offer," one source said.

Defence Minister Sheikh Salem Sabah al-Salem al-Sabah said last week in a written response to a question by an MP that the "decision to accept the British missile was final and the ministry has begun taking necessary measures to conclude the deal".
He told Arab Times newspaper after Tuesday's parliament session the British contract was "a done deal" which had been approved by the country's Higher Council for Defence.
But some 16 MPs have submitted a motion demanding a full parliament debate on the missile deal and a smaller pending one with China for the purchase of mortars, newspapers said.
A defence ministry committee had picked the French Aerospatiale MM-15 missile to arm Kuwait's eight French-made fast patrol boats.
The decision was reversed in favour of British Aerospace's Sea Skua missile which was successfully used during the 1991 Gulf War against Iraqi naval units.
Kuwait's previous parliament last year asked its Public Funds Protection Committee to investigate the deal after the cheaper French offer was dropped.
